content.comment_body: Hello, This is my first time working with a [product_name], mainly for learning purposes. I have just one device: [article_no]. On one side it shows FS:02. After checking the firmware using [product_name], it displays [version_no]. I'm trying to create a program with [product_name] [version_no], but I'm unsure which exact model I have. I assume it's a '[article_no].[version_no] Standard', but I'm not certain. What's the best way to identify a [product_name] device? How can I tell if it is [version_no]? I don't encounter this issue with other controllers like [product_name]. Thank you in advance for your assistance.
I've put together a brief history of the [article_no] [product_name] devices. Please check the attached file.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is uncertain about distinguishing the exact model and firmware version of their [product_name] device, particularly when differentiating among various [article_no] versions and related firmware. This leads to confusion about software compatibility and hardware identification, which contrasts with the straightforward identification process found in other controller series.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes for a simple method to identify the model and firmware version of the [product_name] device, similar to what is available for other controllers, and seeks clear guidance or labeling that would help.
